title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study classes of maps in Fl(Cat), the arrows of the category of small categories, with W the class of weak equivalences (functors inducing homotopy equivalences of nerves). This is the framework of Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs, later written up by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. The page is a bookkeeping sheet: a lattice of classes of functors, the inclusions among them, and their stability under base change. It sets up the analysis of the 'cohomological' (homotopical) behaviour of functors.

The classes:
- F: Grothendieck fibrations (cartesian).
- C: cofibrations (opfibrations, cocartesian).
- B = F∩C: bifibrations.
- Sm: smooth functors.
- Pr: proper functors.
- S: 'Serre maps, i.e. Hot-fibrations'. These are functors whose fibres are homotopy fibres universally, i.e. every pullback square along f is homotopy cartesian; in other words, Quillen quasifibrations.
- T: 'universally in W'.
- WSF, WSC: 'weak Serre' classes. From the inclusions he uses, these must be the Quillen Theorem‑B conditions, read off the inclusions rather than stated on the page:
  - WSF ('Serre fibrations') asks that b\A → b'\A be in W for every arrow b→b'.
  - WSC ('Serre cofibrations') asks that A/b → A/b' be in W.
- WSB: an analogous class modelled on bifibrations. It is presumably a condition involving both slices, e.g. double slices b\A/b'. The page asserts WSB ⊊ WSF∩WSC but does not give the definition.

Relations stated:
1. F ⊂ Sm and C ⊂ Pr (fibrations are smooth, opfibrations proper).
2. Sm∩Pr ⊂ S. Proof sketch: properness gives A_b ≃ A/b; smoothness gives A_b ≃ b\A. Over any arrow Δ1→B both fibre inclusions into the pullback A_{Δ1} are in W. Hence the Theorem‑B condition holds, so fibres are homotopy fibres, and this is stable under base change.
3. WSC∩Pr = S∩Pr and WSF∩Sm = S∩Sm. Properness identifies the fibre with A/b, and Theorem B then makes A/b the homotopy fibre; dually for smooth maps.
4. S ⊂ WSB ⊂ WSF∩WSC, the second inclusion strict ('WSB ≠ WSF∩WSC !').
5. WSF is stable under proper base change; WSC under smooth base change; S under arbitrary base change.
6. Upper diagram: the cube of intersections B; F∩Pr, Sm∩C; F∩S, Sm∩Pr, S∩C; F, Sm∩S, S∩Pr, C; Sm, S, Pr. Its squares are cartesian and its classes are stable under any base change. Intermediate classes are marked strictly between the S‑ and non‑S nodes:
   - F∩S ⊊ F∩WSC ⊊ F, Sm∩S ⊊ Sm∩WSC ⊊ Sm;
   - dually S∩C ⊊ WSF∩C ⊊ C, S∩Pr ⊊ WSF∩Pr ⊊ Pr.
   The 'wrong-sided' intersections C∩WSF and F∩WSC are not contained in S. Example over Δ1: an opfibration A→Δ1 with transition φ: A_0→A_1. Then A ≃ A_1, so b\A → b'\A is in W, but A_0 ≄ A_1 in general.
7. Lower diagram, intersected with W:
   - S∩W = S∩T. A Serre map is a weak equivalence iff its fibres are aspheric, iff it is universally in W.
   - Hence W∩F∩S = T∩F, W∩S∩C = T∩C, W∩Sm∩S = T∩Sm, W∩S∩Pr = T∩Pr, W∩S = T∩S (= 'UW').
   - W∩WSC = As: Quillen‑A aspheric functors, A/b aspheric for all b. Indeed W plus Theorem B forces the homotopy fibre A/b to be contractible, and conversely Theorem A applies.
   - W∩WSF = As°: coaspheric functors, b\A aspheric.
   - W∩WSB = Tot As: 'totally aspheric' functors.
   - Strict chain: W∩S ⊊ Tot As ⊊ As, As° ⊊ W. As is stable under smooth base change, As° under proper base change, W only under S (Serre) base change.
   - He suspects the square Tot As / As / As° / W is NOT cartesian, i.e. Tot As ≠ As∩As°.
8. Open questions:
   - (i) Are WSC and WSB stable under base change along S∩C, even in the 'trivial' case (footnote *)? Concretely: find f ∈ W∩WSB (totally aspheric) and g ∈ T∩C (opfibration with aspheric fibres) whose base change f': X'→Y' is not in WSC. For instance, take Y' with a final object e and y' such that X'_{/y'} → X'_{/e} is not a weak equivalence.
   - (ii) Even when fibres are aspheric, can the Serre condition be tested using only base changes Δ1→X? Answer not given on the page.
9. Bookkeeping: the classes are stable under intersection except for the mixed ones (WSF∩C, WSC∩Pr and duals, WSF∩WSC); likewise for As∩As°.

Purpose: to organise which homotopical properties of functors (Quillen A/B‑type conditions, smoothness and properness) are base‑change stable. This is groundwork for the 'cohomological properties of maps in (Cat)', i.e. a homotopical analogue of smooth/proper base change theorems for functors between small categories.
errors: No outright mathematical error is visible. Several assertions are explicitly marked with '?' (non-stability of WSC/WSB under S∩C base change; Δ1-testability of the Serre condition; non-cartesianness of the As square) and are unresolved on the page.
WSB is never defined on the page (the defining line 'WSB… = def' is overwritten), so the claims WSB ≠ WSF∩WSC and Tot As ≠ As∩As° cannot be checked from this sheet alone.
The struck phrase 'and also iff it is univ. in W' is actually true for Serre maps, since Serre maps are stable under base change; it was presumably struck as redundant with S∩W = S∩T.

The phrase 'stable by intersections except WSF∩C and WSC∩Pr…' is ambiguous: it is unclear whether it means the listed intermediate classes are not intersections of lattice members, or that the class of classes is not closed under ∩.

ideas.what: Fibrations are smooth, opfibrations proper; smooth and proper functors between small categories, defined homotopically
ideas.modern_name: W-smooth / W-proper functors (foncteurs lisses/propres); smooth/proper maps of simplicial sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs), developed by Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006) and Maltsiniotis; ∞-version Lurie HTT §4.1.2
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (circulated manuscript); exposed in Maltsiniotis, Astérisque 301 and Cisinski, Astérisque 308

ideas.what: Smooth ∩ proper ⊂ Serre (quasifibration); Pr∩WSC = Pr∩S and Sm∩WSF = Sm∩S
ideas.modern_name: Proper (resp. smooth) functors satisfying the Quillen Theorem B condition are homotopy-fibre sequences; smooth+proper ⇒ locally constant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Theorem B, 1973) for (co)fibred categories; general smooth/proper form in Cisinski

ideas.what: Serre map is a weak equivalence iff fibres aspheric iff universally a weak equivalence (S∩W = S∩T)
ideas.modern_name: Quasifibration with contractible fibres is a (universal) weak equivalence

ideas.what: W∩(Theorem-B condition on A/b) = aspheric functors (Quillen A); dually coaspheric; stability of aspheric under smooth base change and coaspheric under proper base change
ideas.modern_name: W-aspheric / W-coaspheric functors and their base-change stability

ideas.what: Systematic lattice of 13+ classes (F, C, B, Sm, Pr, S, their intersections, weak-Serre classes WSF/WSC/WSB, and their W-versions As, As°, Tot As) with base-change stability and strict inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Classification of homotopy-fibration-type conditions on functors (Quillen B variants, 'Grothendieck–Serre' fibrations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single standard source; pieces in Cisinski and in the literature on quasifibrations of categories

ideas.what: Bifibration-type weak Serre class WSB and 'totally aspheric' functors Tot As = W∩WSB, strictly smaller than As∩As°
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear ('totally aspheric' in Pursuing Stacks refers to categories, not functors)

ideas.what: Question whether the Serre (quasifibration) property of a functor can be tested by pulling back along arrows Δ1→X only
ideas.modern_name: Local (1-simplex) testability of quasifibrations / Theorem B conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: related: Quillen Theorem B; Thomason; testing along all Δn is standard

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the weak-Serre classes WSC and WSB fail to be stable under base change along Serre opfibrations (S∩C), even when the base change is 'trivial' (opfibration with aspheric fibres) and the map is totally aspheric. He sketches the kind of counterexample sought.
missed.quote: WSC,WSB not stable under S∩C base ch.? (And dually!) even if both are "trivial"? * … find f:X→Y, g:Y'→Y with f∈W∩WSB (i.e. f tot. asph.) and g∈T∩C … s.th. f':X'→Y' is not in WSC
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Base-change stability of Theorem-B-type conditions under fibrations is exactly what is needed for homotopical smooth/proper base change in Cat and ∞-categories. A definite answer, or counterexample, is not standard in the literature as far as I know.

missed.claim: Whether the Serre/quasifibration condition for a functor with aspheric fibres can be detected by base changes along Δ1→X alone.
missed.quote: Even if fibers are aspheric the Serre condition cannot be tested by only taking base-changes Δ1→X ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable question about 1-dimensional testability of homotopy fibre sequences of categories. It is relevant to combinatorial criteria (Quillen B-type) for quasifibrations of nerves.

missed.claim: A complete strict-inclusion lattice relating Grothendieck (op)fibrations, smooth and proper functors, quasifibrations ('Serre maps') and the one-sided Theorem-B classes. It includes the facts that Pr∩WSC = Pr∩S, Sm∩WSF = Sm∩S, and that the wrong-sided intersections (C∩WSF, F∩WSC) are not Serre; also the W-shadow (As, As°, Tot As) with differing base-change stabilities.
missed.quote: WSC∩Pr⊂S, WSF∩Sm⊂S … C∩WSF⊄S ? F∩WSC⊄S ? … Tot As = W∩WSB … As°=W∩WSF (stable by proper b.ch.) As=W∩WSC (stable by smooth b.ch.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Individual pieces are in Cisinski and Maltsiniotis. The organised picture, especially the intermediate 'one-sided Serre' classes and a bifibration-type class WSB distinct from WSF∩WSC, does not appear as such in the literature as far as I know.

missed.claim: The notion of 'totally aspheric' functor (W∩WSB), strictly between Serre weak equivalences and aspheric∩coaspheric, with the conjecture that As∩As° ≠ Tot As.
missed.quote: this square non cartesian? … stable by intersection except As∩As°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would be a new intermediate asphericity notion for functors. It is possibly related to double-slice/twisted-arrow conditions used in modern ∞-categorical cofinality results.

deep.surprise_reason: Most relations are standard or follow from Quillen's Theorem A/B and the Grothendieck–Cisinski theory of smooth/proper functors. The systematic lattice with one-sided weak-Serre classes, the bifibration class WSB ≠ WSF∩WSC, and the open questions (S∩C base-change stability, Δ1-testability) are notable unpublished details. They are not, however, a major result.
transcription_corrections: Top heading appears to read 'WSB∩Sm' (overwritten) rather than 'WSB_n PPB'; matches the parenthetical '(WSB∩Sm)' below.
In 'stable by intersections except WSF∩C and WCF∩Pr' the second term should read WSC∩Pr (the image has 'WCF∩Pr', a slip for WSC∩Pr).
Arrow labels in the upper diagram: 'F∩WSC' on the arrow F∩S→F, 'Sm∩WSC' on the arrow Sm∩S→Sm, 'WSF∩Pr' on S∩Pr→Pr, 'WSF∩C' on S∩C→C. These are intermediate classes, not nodes.
'[-W_2C-] WSC' is an overwritten 'WSC' (Serre cofibrations); '[-B_∘F-]' is an overwritten 'WSF'.
In the lower diagram the left node reads 'W∩F∩S = T∩F' (struck prefix before '=').
'T = "universally in W"' (top right) is the definition of T used in S∩W = S∩T.
